findings.finding: is_can_grab RAISES instead of returning False for bracket-unmatched netlocs: probed `GithubGrabber().is_can_grab("https://[github.com/o/r")` -> ValueError('Invalid IPv6 URL') from urlsplit. Go url.Parse returns an error ("missing ']' in host") and IsCanGrab returns false (grabber.go:34-37), so Go routes the URL to the fallback client grabber while the port crashes the whole fetch. Reachable: the only upstream guard is the http(s):// prefix check (webfetch.go:39-41). Unrecorded: inventory row 29 (HTTP-REGEX) explicitly claims "urlsplit does not raise" — false for bracketed netlocs — and its TODO(port) covers only ASCII control-char stripping. Per rulebook section 5 this is an inventory bug to flag; the implementer reproduced the row's claim verbatim (grabber.py:53-58) without probing it.
findings.citation: Go grabber.go:33-39 (err -> return false); Go webfetch.go:39-41 (prefix-only guard); inventory.tsv row 29 HTTP-REGEX ("urlsplit does not raise" claim + control-char-only TODO); probe 2026-10-27: urlsplit('https://[github.com/o/r') -> ValueError: Invalid IPv6 URL

findings.finding: is_can_grab verdict FLIP on invalid percent-escapes in the path: probed `is_can_grab("https://github.com/o/%2")` and `is_can_grab("https://github.com/%zz")` -> True, because urlsplit does not validate escapes while the host is still exactly 'github.com'. Go url.Parse rejects invalid escapes in the path (setPath -> unescape -> EscapeError), so IsCanGrab returns false (grabber.go:34-37) and Go fetches the ORIGINAL url via the client grabber; the port returns True, Grab() then matches the repo regex ([^/]+ accepts '%2') and fetches a rewritten https://api.github.com/repos/o/%2 URL. Consequence: different URL fetched end-to-end on reachable input. Unrecorded by inventory row 29, whose only special-case discussion is the bare '%zz' string (empty netloc) — not escapes after a valid github.com host.
findings.citation: Go grabber.go:33-37 + grabber_test.go:25 (the Go test's own '%zz -> false' row: url.Parse's only failure mode for that string is escape rejection, proving url.Parse validates percent-escapes); net/url unescape validation applies identically to absolute-URL paths; probe 2026-10-27: is_can_grab('https://github.com/o/%2') == True

findings.finding: Issue regex (\d+) is Unicode-sensitive in Python but ASCII-only in Go: probed _GITHUB_ISSUE_RE.match('https://github.com/o/r/issues/١٢٣') -> match with group(4)='١٢٣' (Python re \d matches any Unicode Nd digit for str patterns). Go RE2 \d is exactly [0-9] (regexp/syntax: \d == [0-9]), so grabber.go:56 nils and Go falls back to the client grabber; the port fetches https://api.github.com/repos/o/r/issues/١٢٣. Same input class as the trailing-\n/$ divergence the inventory explicitly probed and pinned (rows 28/29), but this one is unrecorded — the rows pin 'pattern text translated verbatim EXCEPT $ -> \Z' and rulebook section 2's RE2 row claims 'All in-repo patterns are RE2-safe', which is true of the pattern TEXT but not of char-class semantics. The code matches the row's letter (verbatim text, no re.ASCII), so the fix is an inventory/rulebook amendment (re.ASCII flag or a recorded TODO(port)), not silent acceptance.
findings.citation: Go grabber.go:25 (githubIssueRegex (\d+)); rulebook section 2 RE2 row ('pattern text translated verbatim except Go $ -> Python \Z'; 'All in-repo patterns are RE2-safe'); inventory.tsv rows 28 (NIL-ERR) and 29 (HTTP-REGEX) — verbatim-except-\Z pin; probe 2026-10-27: issue regex matches Arabic-Indic digits, re.match(r'[0-9]+', '١٢٣') is None

findings.finding: The test file omits the ContentGrabber import that inventory row 36 (TEST-FILE) spells in its sanctioned import list ('from websearch.services.webfetch.local.grabber.grabber import ContentGrabber, ...'). The omission is documented in the module docstring (grabber_test.py:3-8) with a defensible rationale — the name is unused in the port and importing it would trip ruff F401 — but the row is the decision and this diverges from its spelled list; flagging for the amendment queue so the row and the file stop disagreeing.

findings.finding: FakeGrabber method spelling 'is_can_grab' diverges from inventory row 37 (TEST-FAKE), which literally spells the mock method 'def is_cangrab(self, resource: Resource) -> bool'. The port uses is_can_grab and documents the conflict in the class docstring (grabber_test.py:191-200). The divergence is forced and correct: row 37 itself requires the mock to 'structurally satisfy the port's ContentGrabber Protocol', whose method is is_can_grab (row 41 IFACE + sibling stub grabber/grabber.py:19), and mypy strict compares method names — a literal 'is_cangrab' mock would fail typecheck as the fallback= argument. Rows 35/37 ('is_cangrab'/'test_is_cangrab') and row 41 ('is_can_grab') are internally inconsistent; the implementer followed each row where it applies (test function name test_is_cangrab per row 35, method is_can_grab per row 41) but the residual row conflict needs an amendment.
findings.citation: inventory.tsv row 37 (TEST-FAKE, literal 'def is_cangrab'); inventory.tsv row 41 (IFACE, Protocol spells is_can_grab); inventory.tsv row 35 (test_is_cangrab); grabber_test.py:44 (test_is_cangrab) vs :206 (is_can_grab); rulebook section 4 lines 166-170 (mypy Protocol name-compatibility note)

adherence: The implementer followed the rulebook and inventory to a high, verifiable degree. Honored pins, each verified against Go source and/or probes: (1) the three routing regexes are byte-verbatim except the sanctioned $->\\Z on the repo pattern (rows 28/29; probed: trailing-\\n URL nils in the port, matches under a naive $), m.group(1..4) per row 28; (2) IsCanGrab userinfo-stripped last-@ netloc.rpartition('@'), case-preserved, :443 kept in the comparison, %zz -> False — all probed verdicts match Go url.Host semantics (row 29); (3) synthesized Content-Type literals text/plain (file) / application/json (repo+issue) with a fresh single-entry lowercased parameters dict, no upstream headers, no value pre-parsing (rows 27/30); (4) UA Firefox on every fetch + Accept vnd.github.v3+json only on json routes (row 29), FF-4 literal byte-identical across rulebook/fingerprint.py/test/judge fixedgo.py; (5) fallback identity return with no copy, no 5MB cap on this path (cap confirmed client-only, client/grabber.go:13), read-before-close try/finally, byte-exact 'request failed with status {code}' (rows 27/32/37); (6) new_grabber signature/return typing matches row 41; nil-deref analogues as adjacent asserts per section 2 Optional-deref row; ctx dropped per row 26. Test file: MockTransport mapping (not httptest) per rows 31/39, all eleven parametrize rows verbatim with id= (rows 31/33/35), stale websearch/1.0 UA replaced by the FF-4 literal per row 34 and section 4 line 154, pytest.raises match for the status error and errors.Is translated as unwrapped-exception identity (row 32; probed: MockTransport propagates the handler's exception object with identity preserved, and httpx merges accept: */* so the row's negation assertion is the right call), zero-value GithubGrabber() construction (row 40), FakeGrabber structurally Protocol-shaped, absolute imports, empty __init__.py files, accurate PORT STATUS trailers (todos=2/0 vs counted markers), no type suppressions (section 3), and ruff lint + format --check pass (the read-only half of the section 0 referee; mypy is denied in-loop and was not run — manual strict-mode scan found no violations). Deviations: five findings above — three divergence-class unrecorded Go-vs-Python semantic gaps at the IsCanGrab/regex site that inventory rows 29/28 claim to have settled (urlsplit ValueError on bracket-unmatched netlocs, invalid percent-escape verdict flips, Unicode \\d in the issue regex), and two cosmetic/ambiguity items (ContentGrabber import omitted from row 36's spelled list; row 37's 'is_cangrab' spelling conflict with the Protocol row). All five are amendment-queue items against the inventory/rulebook as much as against the code: in each case the code matches the row's letter, and the gap is the row's incomplete claim of equivalence. The RequestFailedError class defined locally in grabber.py rather than awaited-from-service.py follows section 2's typed-exception mandate and carries the TODO(port) the UNKNOWN rule requires (counted in the trailer).
